name: Arm Swings
cues: Relax shoulders, ribs down, tall spine
progression: Increase range gradually

name: Torso Twists
cues: Rotate through upper back, hips mostly forward

name: Hip Openers
cues: Relax shoulders, ribs down, tall spine

name: Step Back Lunges
cues: Step back softly. Front heel grounded. Torso tall. Control the return.

name: Inchworms
cues: Slow and controlled. Hinge at hips, crawl out to straight-arm plank and back.

name: Butt Kicks
cues: Relax shoulders, keep posture tall, try to reach heel to butt

name: Lateral Lunges
cues: Drive from heel of bent knee

name: High Knees
cues: Drive knee to hip height. Stay tall. Increase speed only if posture stays controlled.

name: T-Spine Windmills
cues: Obliques, shoulders, spinal rotation

name: Leg Swings
cues: Light support if needed. Swing from hip, not low back. Control both directions.

name: Breathing + Posture Reset
cues: Sit tall. Inhale through nose. Exhale through mouth. Feel tall, shoulders soft.
progression: Eyes closed may help

name: Core Bracing
cues: Zip up a snug jacket around your waist. Breathe normally. Do not hold breath.
progression: Maintain gentle brace during all exercises

name: Seated Marches
cues: Tall posture. Smooth lift. Lift only as high as comfortable.

name: Deadbug
cues: Rest head on floor. Do not let lower back arch when straightening leg.
progression: Add hold at end range

name: Lying Leg Lifts
cues: Start with legs at 90°. Only lower where you can control core with no lower back pain.
progression: Increase range as strength improves

name: Wall Angels
cues: Stand with back flat against wall. Slide arms up and down in Y-T-W pattern.

name: Hip Hinges
cues: Drive hips back. Neutral spine. Squeeze glutes at top.
progression: Add load when pattern is solid

name: Grip + Hand Health
cues: Squeeze: firm grip, no pain. Pinch & Roll. Palm Massage. Wrist Circles. Keep what feels good.

name: Shoulder Blade Squeezes
cues: Back and down. No shrug. Pause + squeeze back (not up).
progression: Hold each squeeze 3–4 seconds

name: Band Rotation (Rotator Cuff)
cues: Elbow stays glued to your side. Rotate forearm outward. Reduce band tension if too hard.
progression: Progress to 3 sets

name: Band Pull-Apart
cues: Ribs down, don't shrug. Arms straight out front, pull band apart.
progression: Slow 3 sec out, 2 sec hold

name: Band Leg Extensions
cues: Smooth. Don't snap the band. Band around ankle, anchor to chair leg, extend knee forward slowly.
coachingFocus: Focus on the extension, feeling the upper thigh muscles working.
progression: Lighter band or smaller range if too hard

name: Seated Dumbbell Row
cues: Pull with the elbow, not the hand. Hinge slightly forward.
progression: 1–2 reps before adding weight

name: Seated Bicep Curl
cues: Smooth and controlled. Sitting tall, curl weights to shoulder.
progression: Too hard? Use one dumbbell

name: Straight Leg Circles
cues: Small circles. Keep quad tight.
progression: Make circles smaller if too hard

name: Pushups Against the Wall
cues: Core engaged, don't let hips drop. Hands below shoulder height. Adjust to avoid wrist pain.
progression: Move hands/ball lower to increase difficulty

name: Bicep Curls
cues: keep elbows close to body, don't go all the way to the top - leave space so you can feel the weight and the extension and contraction.
progression: Add reps before adding weight

name: DB Tricep Kickbacks
cues: Elbows locked to side. Elbows above body height. Neutral spine — look 45° down.
progression: Stay in deep lunge for additional challenge

name: Reverse Flys
cues: Arms straight in front. Pull back, widen hands, squeeze elbows behind to activate upper back.

name: Machine Lat Pulldowns
cues: Pull bar on angle toward chin. Squeeze elbows toward waist. Control return.
progression: Increase load when form is solid

name: DB Chest Press
cues: Control descent. Pause at chest. Drive up.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Bent Over Row
cues: Hinge at hips. Pull elbows back. Squeeze shoulder blades.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: DB Flys — Flat Bench
cues: Wide arc with slight elbow bend. Feel chest stretch at bottom but don't go too low, keep the elbow bend.
coachingFocus: Smaller chest muscles and anterior deltoids.
contraindications: Lighten the weight if you feel too much strain on the side of your shoulders.
progression: Lighten the weight or add weight.

name: Lat Pullovers
cues: Keep slight elbow bend. Feel lat stretch at top.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Plié Squats
cues: Toes out on a 45 degree angle. Knees tracking over toes. Keep your body upright, and pretend you are pressing your "sit bones" toward the ground, pressing knees outward as you come down.
coachingFocus: Stabilizer muscles for adductors and abductors
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Single-Leg Deadlift
cues: Hinge from hip. Maintain long spine. Working leg soft.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Hamstring Curls on Ball
cues: Bridge first then curl. Control the extension.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Skull Crushers
cues: Elbows in. Only forearm moves. Controlled descent.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Seated Shoulder Press
cues: Start at ear height. Press overhead. Don't arch lower back.
progression: Rest 30 sec

name: Box Jumps
cues: Knees soft. Use arms to lift. Bend knees on landing. Start with lower box.
progression: Do not work through knee pain

name: Standing Long Jumps
cues: Light bounce to prepare. Land on whole foot. Knees soft.

name: Oblique Med Ball Throw
cues: Core fully engaged — especially obliques. Shoulders braced. Swing from middle, throw on angle upward at wall.
progression: Start light — med balls don't bounce

name: Ball Bounce
cues: Hinge at hips, eyes tracking ball. React to bounce — dont anticipate. Keep knees soft.
progression: Vary drop height and distance from body

name: Wall Throw
cues: Stand arm-length from wall. Throw with one hand, catch with both. Eyes stay on ball.
progression: Single-hand catch, add reaction colour cue

name: Left-Right Toss
cues: Toss hand to hand. Cross midline. Eyes track ball, not hands. Tall posture throughout.
progression: Add counting backward, colour naming, or single-leg stance

name: Ball Toss and Talk
cues: Match stance to your level: seated, single-leg, walking, or dual-task. Ball tracks midline.
progression: Progress through seated → single-leg → walking → dual-task with colour/number cue

name: DB Bicep Curl
cues: Elbows stay at sides. Full range of motion — extend fully at bottom. Control the descent.
progression: Add weight when 12 reps feel fully controlled

name: Gorilla Rows
cues: Legs wider than hip width, kettlebells inside legs. Back flat, core engaged. Elbows tight to body. Alternate rows — brace hard on the support side.
progression: Increase KB weight when form is solid for all 20 reps

name: Plyo Incline Push-Ups
cues: Hands on bench, body in straight plank. Lower with control then push explosively. Lightly lift hands off bench at top of each rep.
progression: Full floor push-up with clap between reps

name: Medicine Ball Smash
cues: Both feet parallel, slight bend in knees. Hold ball with palms, elbows bent. Stand close to wall. Push and smash ball at wall quickly — grab it immediately on rebound.
progression: 4 sets of 10 with heavier medicine ball

name: Weight Plate Walking Lunges
cues: Relax traps — they engage naturally. Core fully engaged, breathing concentrated. Keep arms as straight as possible overhead. Can pause at each step or move continuously.
progression: Heavier plate, or continuous walking without stop

name: Lunge Tricep Kickbacks
cues: Lean forward in lunge position. Elbows stay above body, hugged close to sides. Upper arm is fixed — only the elbow straightens. Do not swing upper arm away from body.
progression: Increase weight or add a pause at full extension

name: Lateral Arm Raises
cues: Stand tall, ribs down. Soft bend in elbows. Lift arms out to the side toward shoulder height. Lower slowly with control.
progression: Add very light weight only when fully pain-free at shoulder height

name: Front Raises
cues: Stand tall, ribs down. Soft bend in elbows. Raise arms straight in front. Stop before shoulder height. Lower slowly.
progression: Increase range only when pain-free. Stay below your pain threshold

name: Robots
cues: Keep arms low to start. Palms facing outward. Keep elbows at comfortable level as you turn palms down. NO pain. Stay low and work slow.
progression: Goal image is the end point — not the starting point. Progress gradually

name: Chest Taps
cues: Keep bicep and elbow close to body. Palm facing chest. Tap across body. Try for 10 each side. Do not swing arm outward to tap.
progression: Increase range only when movement is pain-free and controlled

name: Chest/Deltoid Stretch
cues: Start with your good arm first. Test slowly how far you can reach without pain. Goal is to have both arms back and pull elbows toward spine.
progression: Do not force range — test your pain threshold to find your pain-free limit

name: Internal/External Rotations
cues: Lie on your side on a bench or floor. Keep elbow against your side as you raise your fist. Internal to external rotation. No pain.
progression: Do not use weight until you have no pain through full range of motion

name: Wall Push-Ups
cues: Engage core before beginning. Hands below shoulder height. Bend elbows and let body weight move toward wall — even one inch at a time. No pain only.
progression: Move closer to wall to make easier. Move feet back as you improve

name: Lateral Shoulder Mobility
cues: Press back against wall. Hold arms out straight at shoulder height. Keep one arm pressed to wall while the other crosses to touch the inside of the opposite arm.
progression: Increase range as mobility improves — always pain-free

name: Single-Leg Bridge
cues: Start with both feet on floor. Lift hips as high as you can with no back pain. When stable, lift one leg and hold 10 seconds. Keep hips level.
progression: If back pain or hamstring cramp occurs, lower hips. Progress to full bridge before single-leg

name: Seated Straight Leg Lifts
cues: Sit tall at 90 degrees with straight back and straight legs. Hands beside you for support. Sit against a wall for better posture. Engage core and lift one leg without bending the knee, then alternate.
progression: Goal is to sit fully upright at 90 degrees — hamstring flexibility is required. Use wall support until posture improves

name: Russian Twists
cues: Use a medicine ball or kettlebell. Keep heels on ground to protect your back. Rotate slowly through full range of motion. Keep core braced throughout.
progression: Lift feet off floor for added challenge when back is fully protected

name: Cable Band Chops
cues: Anchor band at high point. Kneel and pull band diagonally down across body. Core must be fully engaged. Rotate from trunk, not arms.
progression: Move further from anchor or double up band if resistance is too light

name: Band Internal-External Rotation
cues: Use a band with enough resistance to feel the work. Keep elbows and biceps close to sides throughout. Rotate internally then externally with control.
progression: Increase band resistance only when full range is pain-free and controlled

name: Weighted Side Bends
cues: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, stand tall. Alternate leaning as far as you can to each side. Pause between sides to reset posture. Core stays engaged.
progression: Increase weight when full range is controlled with good posture

name: Advanced Weighted Side Bends
cues: One KB pressed overhead, one held at side. Lean toward the lowered side with full control. Overhead arm stays locked. Core fully braced.
progression: Progress from double KB side bends. Increase overhead weight gradually

name: Scapular Push-Ups
cues: Hold a straight-arm plank. Press shoulders away from ears — spread shoulder blades apart (protraction). Then let go and squeeze shoulder blades together (retraction). Repeat with control.
progression: Progress to full push-up range when scapular control is strong

name: Olympic Bar Deadlifts
cues: Hinge at hips. Core strong throughout. Back flat — neutral spine. Drive through heels to stand. Do not overlift — perfect form over heavy weight. Stop if you feel back pain beyond normal muscle work.
progression: Ask for coaching before increasing weight. Form must be perfect before progressing

name: Landmine Rows
cues: Hinge forward with flat back. Pull the end of the bar toward your hip. Elbow stays close to body. If you feel too much in your lower back, stagger one foot back slightly.
progression: Stagger stance reduces lower back load. Increase weight when form is solid

name: Band Lateral Leg Lifts - Female
cues: Make sure you stand straight and not lean to the side. Lift as high as you can while balancing on the other leg.
contraindications: Don't work through unreasonable hip pain.
progression: Don't lift leg as high if it is too difficult.

name: Band Lat Pulldowns
cues: Make sure the band is tight at shoulder-width apart, pull hands away as you pull down - on an angle toward your chin, not straight down.
contraindications: Don't do this if you have trouble holding shoulders above head.
progression: Reduce band tension

name: Forearm Pike
cues:
Keep shoulders stacked over elbows
Let your tailbone reach toward the ceiling
Lift from your core, not by pushing from your feet
Move slow and controlled back to plank
coachingFocus: In step 1 make sure your shoulders are stacked directly above your elbows. Lift - tailbone to ceiling.
contraindications: Any shoulder or low back pain, stop
progression: Do a forearm plank with no pike.

name: Heel Taps
coachingFocus: Look upward not at your knees
contraindications: if you have neck pain, rest your head on the floor instead or support your head.

name: Penguins
cues:
Cues
Shoulders off: Lift blades; keep lower back glued.
Look straight up; keep neck neutral.
Side-to-side: Pendulum motion; bend waist, don’t rotate.
Exhale on tap: Breathe out at every heel touch.

name: Bicycle Crunch
cues:
Lower back glued to the floor.
Lift blades; don't pull your neck.
Eyes to the ceiling
Armpit to knee: Focus on rotation, not just elbows.
Extend long: Reach the opposite leg out straight.
Exhale on twist: Breathe out as you rotate.

name: Forearm Plank
cues:
Cues: 
Place elbows under shoulders and actively push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades.
Tuck your tailbone and pull your ribs toward your hips to slightly round your lower back.
Tighten your glutes and core as if someone is about to punch your stomach.
Keep your gaze on the floor for a long neck and maintain steady, deep breaths.

name: Crunch
cues:
Press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Reach your hands toward your knees while keeping your eyes on the ceiling for a neutral neck.
Exhale as you lift your shoulder blades, sliding your hands toward your knees to shorten the gap between ribs and hips.
Pause at the top for a peak contraction, then slowly lower without letting your shoulders touch the mat.

name: Reverse Crunch
cues:
Knees bent at 90 degrees and press your lower back into the floor.
Place your arms flat by your sides for stability and keep your eyes on the ceiling.
Exhale as you curl your hips toward your chest, peeling your tailbone off the floor using only your abs.
Slowly lower your hips back down without arching your back or using momentum.

name: Candlestick
cues:
Push your heels straight up toward the ceiling, not over your head.
Use only your lower abs to lift your tailbone off the floor.
Avoid swinging your legs; keep the movement controlled and vertical.
Lower your hips back down slowly without letting your back arch.

name: Hollow Body Hold
cues:
Press lower back into the floor; tuck tailbone to round.
Reach arms overhead and hover legs just off the floor.
Shape like a Banana: Keep your shoulder blades and heels lifted; back stays glued.
Breathe shallow and keep everything braced like a rock.

name: Side Plank
cues:
Elbow directly under shoulder; body in a straight line.
Hip Lift: Push hips high toward the ceiling; don't let them sag.
Shoulders Back: Keep chest open and eyes forward; don't rotate downward.
Tighten the obliques closest to the floor throughout the hold.

name: Mountain Climbers
cues:
Hands under shoulders; body like a board.
Knee to Chest: Pull one knee toward your chest without lifting your hips.
Flat Back: Keep your tailbone tucked; don't let your lower back arch.
Light Feet: Switch legs quickly but keep your core steady and quiet.

name: Bird-Dog
cues:
Quadruped Position: Start on hands and knees with a neutral, flat back.
Diagonal Reach: Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously until level with torso.
Hip Square: Don't let your hips tilt; keep your navel pulled toward your spine.
Stable Core: Avoid arching your back at the top; focus on length, not height

name: Commando Plank (Plank Up-Downs)
cues:
Active Transition: Move from forearm plank to high plank one hand at a time.
Hips Quiet: Keep your hips as still as possible; no swaying or rocking.
Core Braced: Maintain the "tuck" and "ribs to hips" throughout the move.
Hand Position: Place your hand exactly where your elbow was for stability.

name: Spiderman Plank
cues:
High Plank Base: Start in a solid high plank with a flat back.
Knee to Elbow: Pull your knee out to the side toward your elbow.
Side Crunch: Squeeze your oblique as the knee moves forward.
Stay Low: Keep your hips level with your shoulders; don’t let them pop up.

name: Flutter Kicks
cues:
Lower back must stay glued to the floor at all times.
Shoulders Up: Lift your head and blades to help keep the back flat. Eyes to ceiling
Small Kicks: Rapidly flutter your legs up and down just above the floor.
Toes Pointed: Keep legs straight and core tight to avoid hip flexor strain.

name: Bear Crawl Hold
cues:
All Fours: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders.
Lift your knees just 2 inches off the floor.
Flat Tabletop: Keep your back perfectly flat; don't let the "table" tilt.
Pull your navel in hard and breathe into the tension.

name: Windshield Wipers
cues:
T-Position: Lie on your back, arms out wide for support, legs straight up.
Side Sweep: Lower your legs to one side while keeping both shoulders down.
Core Pull: Use your obliques to pull the legs back to the center.
Controlled Arc: Move slowly; don't let gravity take over at the bottom.

name: Superman
cues:
Face Down: Lie on your belly with arms and legs extended.
The Lift: Exhale and lift your chest, arms, and legs simultaneously off the floor.
Glute Squeeze: Squeeze your glutes to protect your lower back as you lift.
Long Neck: Keep your gaze down at the mat to avoid neck strain.

name: Plank Jacks
cues:
Plank Base: Start in a forearm or high plank with a tucked tailbone.
Light Jump: Jump your feet out wide and then back together like a jumping jack.
Steady Hips: Keep your hips at the same height; don't let them bounce up and down.
Stay Rigid: Maintain your "ribs to hips" connection to keep your spine stable.

name: Reverse Plank Marches
cues:
Palm Support: Sit with legs long; place hands behind you, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Hips to Sky: Press through heels and palms to lift your hips into a straight line.
The March: Slowly lift one knee toward your chest while keeping your hips level and high.
No Sagging: Exhale on the lift; don't let your butt drop toward the floor as you switch legs.

name: TRX Knee Tucks
cues:
High plank start: Hands under shoulders; feet suspended in loops.
Drive knees: Pull both knees toward your chest together.
Hips up: Lift your hips slightly as you crunch in.
Slow return: Extend back to plank without sagging your back.

name: TRX Plank
cues:
Imprint core: Tuck your tailbone and pull ribs toward your hips.
Active push: Drive your forearms into the floor; don't sag.
No sawing: Keep your feet perfectly still in the suspended loops.
Long neck: Look at the floor to keep your spine neutral.

name: TRX Pike
cues:
Straight legs: Keep knees locked; move only from the hips.
Vertical drive: Use your abs to pull your tailbone to the sky.
Look back: Tuck your head between your arms at the top.
Total control: Lower your hips slowly back to a flat plank.

name: TRX Fallout
cues:
Hollow body: Keep your tailbone tucked and ribs down throughout.
Lean & reach: Roll your hands forward until arms are overhead.
Brace hard: Don't let your lower back arch as you lean.
Pull back: Use your core and arms to return to standing.

name: TRX Hamstring Curls
cues:
Hips high: Keep your glutes squeezed and hips off the mat.
Heels to glutes: Pull the straps toward you using your hamstrings.
Stable base: Keep your arms flat on the floor for balance.
Slow return: Extend your legs slowly without dropping your hips.

name: TRX Suspended Lunge
cues:
Stay upright: Keep your chest up and gaze forward for balance.
90-degree front: Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Drive through heel: Use your standing (barefoot) foot to push up.
Controlled drop: Sink slowly into the lunge to protect your knee.

name: TRX Y-Fly
cues:
Arms straight: Keep a slight bend but don't use your biceps to pull.
Lead with knuckles: Open your arms into a wide "Y" overhead.
Proud chest: Keep your chest up; don't lean your head forward.
Tension always: Don't let the straps go slack at the bottom.

name: TRX Rows
cues:
Body like a board: Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze blades: Pull your chest up and pinch your shoulder blades.
Elbows in: Keep elbows close to your ribs as you pull.
Control the lean: Move slowly; don't let your hips sag.

name: TRX Chest Press
cues:
Strong plank: Keep your body rigid; don't let the lower back arch.
Hollow body: Tuck your tailbone and brace your core throughout.
No strap rub: Keep the straps slightly away from your arms.
Press away: Push through your palms to return to the start.

name: TRX Atomic Push-Up
cues:
Deep push-up: Keep your core tight as you lower your chest.
Crunch in: Pull both knees to your chest after the push-up.
Flat back: Don't let your hips sag during the transition.
Flowing move: Combine the push and the tuck into one fluid set.

name: Golf - Lunge Twist
cues: When you are in a lunge, only twist the ball from the centre of your body and the direction over the leg that is in front.
progression: If you lose balance, try to use a lighter medicine ball.

name: Golf - Standing Band Twists
cues: Keep your arms straight, think of spinal rotation to keep your form.
progression: Reduce band tension if too difficult.

name: Golf - Single Leg Balance
cues: Use the club with very little tension - just light fingertip to balance.
coachingFocus: Focus on core, glutes and keep eyes forward.

name: Air Squats
cues: Keep your weight on your heels and your chin and chest up looking straight ahead to keep your posture.
contraindications: If you feel pain in your knees, try not to go as low.
progression: if it is too difficult, try doing a wall sit instead.

name: Knee Pushups
cues: Make sure your hands are stacked below your shoulders and not in front. Keep your core engaged so your lower back doesn't dip.
progression: If you have difficulty or pain, try a wall pushup instead.

name: Lunge with Hammer Curls
cues: Tip: when your knees are bent, so are your elbows. Use the back leg to push you up and down, while keeping your weight on the front heel as well.

name: Pendulums
cues: Keep your eyes on the ground below your hands - visualize a ball.

name: Bicep Hammer Curls
cues: Keep your elbows tight to your body.
contraindications: Avoid pain in elbows
progression: Reduce weight

name: Rowing Machine
cues: Use it as a warmup or for performance! A very versatile exercise!
coachingFocus: Be very aware of your form.

name: Burpees
progression: Go slowly if you are not ready for plyometrics

name: Olympic Bar Squat
cues: Make sure your body weight is on your heels, keep pelvis tucked to keep back strong, proper form and breathing is extremely important.
contraindications: stop immediately if you feel back pain
progression: reduce weight if you have pain.

name: 2Tier Step-ups
cues: This is a great exercise for agility, speed, coordination - and Anaerobic energy system. Try to work in your 80% + training zone
contraindications: Slow down if you feel light headed.

name: High Knee Step-Ups
cues: This works balance, core, cardio, adductors.
coachingFocus: Make sure you have your whole foot on the bench, bring opposite knee into your chest.

name: Single Leg Wall Sit
cues: Make sure you place your foot so that your knee is bent without your foot behind the knee. Press your back into the wall and weight on your heels.
coachingFocus: Working on adductor strength, balance, core.
contraindications: Don't go lower than 90 degrees
progression: Move up higher if knees bother you.

name: Tricep Pushups - Knees
cues: Keep your elbows tucked close to your body. Keep your pelvis tilted so your low back doesn't sink
contraindications: This is a difficult exercise. Try not to go too low if you are not ready.
progression: Do not work through any pain with shoulders.

name: DB Turkish Getup
cues: Make sure your elbow is directly below your shoulder joint, make sure the bent knee has enough space that it is more at a 90 degree angle so you have room later to move.
coachingFocus: This is an amazing whole body exercise but form is of utmost concern.
contraindications: Make sure you stack your shoulders properly and focus on form.
progression: Reduce weight if you cannot keep good form

name: Turkish Getup
cues: Be sure to stack your elbow directly below your shoulder, the bent knee should be almost 90 degrees, and not have the heel too close to glutes, leaving space to finish the moves.
contraindications: Wait until your form is good before adding weight.

name: Dumbell Stationary Lunges
cues: Use the back leg as your "kickstand" and use the heel on the front leg to press into the ground, bend the back knee to allow the front knee to bend, make sure you check your form before starting.
contraindications: If you have knee pain, reduce your Range of Motion
progression: Lighten the weight or use no weights

name: Jen - OB Deadlift
cues: Tuck pelvis so you engage your core, keep a neutral spine, hinge at hips and use your heels.
contraindications: form is extremely important to avoid back pain or injury.
progression: Lighten the load if you have pain. Use chalk or the hooks.

name: Jen-Hex Bar Squat
cues: keep feet straight, legs wider than hip-width, drive with your heels, use hooks if grip slows you down.

name: Bosu Step Ups
cues:
Stand tall, with good posture.
Step to the very top of the Bosu - with your whole foot.
contraindications: If you are recovering from injury, start slowly and use a counter/bar if needed.
progression: If you feel knee, ankle or foot pain, move off the Bosu. If you want to increase intensity, run up and down instead of step-ups.

name: Weighted Single-Leg Torso Twists
cues: Always turn toward the knee that is up. If you cannot keep form without touching the floor, just tap the floor between reps.
progression: Reduce weight

name: Weighted Woodchoppers
cues: You can increase Range of Motion by lifting the weight up with straight arms and bending one knee to have more movement. Otherwise, concentrate on spinal rotation.
progression: reduce weight or progress with heavier weights and wider ROM

name: Pec Dec
cues: You can do this with or without weights for mobility. For strength make sure you can keep your elbows up with the weight.
contraindications: Do not work through any shoulder pain.
progression: Try without weights if you cannot keep form.

name: Wall Sit with Pilates Ball
cues: Make sure you press your bodyweight into the wall and your knees stay behind your toes. Squeeze the ball to activate your adductors. Try a 10 second hold at the end to feel the muscle work in an isometric hold.
coachingFocus: Stability for adductors and isometric for quads and glutes
contraindications: If you have knee pain, try not to bend as far down, or get a larger ball to avoid inner knee pain.
progression: Add weight for progression, remove ball for regression

name: Single Leg Balance
cues: stand in front of a mirror if you can - stare at your nose and keep your posture as tall as you can.

name: Machine Chest Press
cues: Sit tall with your core engaged before you press forward. Pay attention to feeling your chest working and the front of your shoulders assisting.
contraindications: stop if you feel shoulder pain
progression: Reduce weight if you feel any pain.

name: Machine - Pec Dec
coachingFocus: This exercise is to build strength for the smaller muscles in your chest with some assistance from your shoulders.

name: Band Lateral Leg Lifts
cues: Make sure you pay attention to your posture and stand stall and straight and allow your hips and glutes to work.

name: Band Deadlift Introduction
cues: Make sure you have the band very tight so you can feel the tension when you lift, keep your back as "flat"/straight as you can, lift your tailbone to the ceiling, and think of feeling your hamstrings and lower back but only mildly.
coachingFocus: To work on hamstring flexibility and lower back tension.

name: DB Pec Dec
cues: Keep your elbows the same height as your shoulders. Try to press your elbows together in front of you.
contraindications: Do not work through shoulder pain
progression: Use less weight or no weight.

name: DB Calf Raises
cues: Keep your arms relaxed and shoulders down, with your core engaged, standing tall.
contraindications: If you feel pain please stop.
progression: Try without weights and if you need to hold onto something to keep your posture, it is better than leaning to one side.

name: Cable Machine Tricep Pressdowns - Flat Bar
cues: Keep your elbows tight to your body and right at your side. Don't move the upper part of your arm when you press or release the bar.
coachingFocus: Triceps - back of your arms, bracing your core.
contraindications: If you lose form it is too heavy - if you move your upper arm it is not correct.
progression: Reduce weight if you cannot keep form.

name: Machine Hamstring Curl
progression: If you feel your lower back or a cramp in your hamstring, please reduce the weight - or stop if your back hurts.
